chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mawsili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was your Lord?'

He said: Woe to you! "When was it?" is only asked about something that did not exist. But as for that which always was, you cannot say "when was it?" — He was before the "before" without there being a "before," and after the "after" without there being an "after," and there is no end-point of a limit for His limit to reach.

Then [the rabbi] said to him: Are you a prophet? He said: For your mother be bereavement! I am but a servant from among the servants of the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

key_terms.الْهَبَلُ: Bereavement/grief — a classical Arabic exclamation formula
key_terms.حِبْر: Rabbi/scholar (hibr): a term for a learned Jewish religious authority
key_terms.قَبْلَ الْقَبْلِ بِلَا قَبْلٍ: Before the before without a before — apophatic expression of divine eternity
key_terms.مَتَى كَانَ: When was it? — the temporal question applied to God's pre-existence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when asked when God existed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a remarkable encounter in which a Jewish rabbi challenged Imam Ali (AS) by asking when God began to exist — a question reflecting a temporal framework that conceives of God as having a beginning. Imam Ali's response articulates a sophisticated apophatic theology: the question 'when' presupposes non-existence prior to existence, but God is eternally self-subsistent, transcending the very categories of 'before' and 'after.' When the astonished rabbi asks if he is a prophet, Imam Ali humbly identifies himself as a servant of the Prophet (SAWW), deflecting any suggestion of prophetic status while demonstrating the depth of divinely-inherited wisdom.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Abu Al Hassan Al Mowsaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A Rabbi from the Rabbis came over to Amir Al-Momineenasws and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! When was yourasws Lordazwj (from)?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you! But rather, it is said, ‘When was it’, for what did not happen to be. So, as for what always was, so you cannot say when it was (from). He<sup>azwj</sup> was before the ‘before’ without there being a ‘before’, and (will be) after the ‘after’ without there being an ‘after’, and there is no termination to an end-point to end His<sup>azwj</sup> end-point’.

So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Are you<sup>asws</sup> a Prophet<sup>as</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For your mother be the bereavement! But rather, I<sup>asws</sup> am a servant from the servants of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from ibn Abu Nasr from Abul Hassan al-Muwsali who has narrated the following from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.).
“A rabbi hibr came to Imam Ali (a.s.) and asked, ‘O Amirul Mu’minin, when did your Lord come into existence?’”

Imam Ali (a.s.) replied, “Consider carefully. The question When applies to one who did not exist (and then came into being). When does not apply to the One Who is eternal. He was before the before without before and after the after without an after. He is not the end of some end so that His end would also end.”
He then asked, “Are you a prophet?” Imam Ali (a.s.) replied, “Bereft of you be your mother! I am a salve among the slaves of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.).”
